findings: Isolated Host direct-post (no concurrent Windows matrix or controls) reproduced the timeout 3/3 before the 1-hour Type lock expired (attempt 2 run records: status error, adapter-failure, 'module ifx-database-evidence timed out.'); host workspace evidence production alone took 70-72 s.

The ifx-database-evidence adapter run alone in the same container passes every time but needs 84-85 s (direct scan) and 73-74 s (with Host workspace evidence) against the declared 60 s module timeout.
The workload is identical to 0.4.2: the database source inventory has the same 1152 files and 138 lock files, and the module bytes are identical.
A same-day 0.4.2 baseline could not be timed: its 24-hour database lock has expired, so its adapter stops at the staleness check.
conclusion: Not caused by 0.4.3 content. The 60 s timeout of ifx-database-evidence is too tight for Linux container file I/O over a Windows bind mount on this machine today; the 0.4.2 run's margin was not recorded. Windows (the IFX product platform) passes. Linux remains a non-blocking advisory under C6c22, and the Linux compatibility bridge stays required (P10.3).
followUp: A later bundle version could raise or platform-scale the ifx-database-evidence timeout after measurement; this needs its own Plan and is outside T7.
